intro.title: From one hill town to half the known world
body: Legend says Rome was founded in 753 BC by Romulus. For centuries it was one small city among many in central Italy, first under kings, then as a republic run by elected magistrates and an aristocratic Senate.

Over 500 years it conquered Italy, then Carthage, Greece, Gaul and Egypt. The Republic tore itself apart in civil wars, and Augustus turned it into an empire ruled by one man. At its height under Trajan, the empire stretched from Scotland to the Persian Gulf.

Then came crisis, recovery, division into East and West, and the slow loss of the western provinces to Germanic peoples. In AD 476 the last western emperor was deposed. The eastern half carried on for almost another thousand years.
tips: Press play and watch the red spread across the map, century by century.
From AD 395 the empire splits: red is the West, wine-red the East. Watch the West break up into barbarian kingdoms.
The Siege of Alesia has an animated close-up. For Cannae and Hannibal, follow the link to the Rome v Carthage story.

eras.title: The kings
eras.text: Seven legendary kings rule a small city by the Tiber, under strong Etruscan influence.

eras.title: The Republic conquers Italy
eras.text: Rome expels its last king, survives a Gallic sack, and fights Latins, Samnites, Etruscans and Pyrrhus until it rules Italy.

eras.title: Mediterranean empire
eras.text: Three wars with Carthage and wars against the Greek kingdoms make Rome master of the Mediterranean.

eras.title: Fall of the Republic
eras.text: Reformers murdered, generals with private armies, civil wars. Caesar wins, is killed, and his heir takes everything.

eras.title: Pax Romana
eras.text: Two centuries of relative peace under the emperors. The empire reaches its greatest size under Trajan.

eras.title: Crisis
eras.text: Civil wars, plague, invasions and breakaway empires. Over 20 emperors in 50 years.

eras.title: The late empire
eras.text: Diocletian and Constantine rebuild the state. Christianity rises and a new capital is founded at Constantinople.

eras.title: Fall of the West
eras.text: The empire divides for good. Goths, Vandals and Huns carve up the West until its last emperor is deposed.

ask.persona: a vivid, careful historian of ancient Rome who explains its rise and fall to a curious listener. You point out when stories are legend rather than history, when numbers are ancient estimates, and when historians disagree, for example about why the western empire fell
defaultQuestions: Why did this matter for Rome's rise or fall?
